statement: A sheet of paper is cut into 3 pieces. Then one of the pieces is cut into 3 pieces, then one of the pieces is cut into 3, and so on: each cut turns one piece into 3. After 20 cuts in total, how many pieces are there?

choices.misconception: I thought each cut makes 3 pieces, so 20 cuts make 3 x 20.
I added 3 pieces for every cut to the 1 sheet I started with.
I saw that each cut adds 2 pieces but forgot to count the sheet I started with.
I thought each cut adds one more piece, as when a piece is cut in two.

hints: Count the pieces after 1, 2 and 3 cuts.
Try small cases first: work out the number of pieces after the first few cuts and look at how much each cut changes the count. Then extend that pattern to 20 cuts.
After 1 cut there are 3 pieces, after 2 cuts 5, after 3 cuts 7. Each cut removes one piece and adds three.

solutions.reliable: Small cases: 0 cuts give 1 piece, 1 cut gives 3, 2 cuts give 5, 3 cuts give 7. Each cut takes away one piece and puts back three, a gain of 2. After 20 cuts there are 1 + 2 x 20 = 41 pieces. The transferable idea: when a process repeats many times, run it two or three times by hand and find how much each step changes the count.
solutions.elegant: The number of pieces is always odd and grows by 2 each cut, so after n cuts it is 2n + 1, and 2 x 20 + 1 = 41.

whyOnTest: Large repeated processes are a signal to try small cases first; the traps are counting pieces made instead of pieces gained, or forgetting the start.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
